newsitem.title: USA: Oregon legislator proposes budget 'rainy day' fund.
newsitem.headline: Oregon legislator proposes budget 'rainy day' fund.

text.p: Oregon House Speaker Lynn Lundquist will introduce legislation in the coming days that would create a state "rainy day" fund for use in economic downturns, a spokeswoman said Thursday.
Under the speaker's proposal, surplus state revenues would be placed in a reserve account earmarked for education, spokeswoman Margaret Hunt said.
The legislation would prevent the fund from accumulating to more than seven percent of total general fund dollars. Any surplus beyond that cap would be returned to taxpayers.
The rainy day funds could be appropriated only at times of economic strain, such as when nonfarm employment declines for two consecutive quarters or when a budget deficit is projected, Hunt said.

"This rainy day fund would have been a lifesaver in the early 1980s when Oregon suffered the worst economic downturn since the Great Depression," the Republican Speaker said in a statement. "We need an insurance policy so that our schools are not devastated in a recession."
If approved by state lawmakers, Lundquist's proposal would be placed on the ballot.
